verses.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖੀਆ ਦੁਸਟੁ ਦੁਬਾਜਰਾ ਤਾਮੇ ਰੰਗਹੁ ਕੈਹਾ ਹੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: dhukheeaa dhusaT dhubaajaraa taame ra(n)gahu kaihaa hovai|

en.bdb: The evil double-talker is copper which looks like bronze.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬਾਹਰੁ ਦਿਸੈ ਉਜਲਾ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਮਸੁ ਨ ਧੋਪੈ ਧੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: baahar dhisai ujalaa a(n)dhar mas na dhopai dhovai|

en.bdb: Apparently, the bronze looks bright but even persisting washing cannot clean its inner blackness.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸੰਨੀ ਜਾਣੁ ਲੁਹਾਰ ਦੀ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਮੂਹੀਂ ਕੁਸੰਗ ਵਿਗੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: sa(n)nee jaan luhaar dhee hoi dhumoohee(n) kusa(n)g vigovai|

en.bdb: The pliers of blacksmith is double mouthed but being in the bad company (of the blacksmith) it destroys itself.

verses.gurmukhi: ਖਿਣੁ ਤਤੀ ਆਰਣਿ ਵੜੈ ਖਿਣੁ ਠੰਢੀ ਜਲੁ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਟੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: khin tatee aaran vaRai khin Tha(n)ddee jal a(n)dhar Tovai|

en.bdb: It goes in the hot furnance and the next moment it is put in cold water.

verses.gurmukhi: ਤੁਮਾ ਦਿਸੇ ਸੋਹਣਾ ਚਿਤ੍ਰਮਿਤਾਲਾ ਵਿਸੁ ਵਿਲੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: tumaa dhise sohanaa chitramitaalaa vis vilovai|

en.bdb: The colocynth gives a beautiful, piebald look but inside it remains poison.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਾਉ ਨ ਕਉੜਾ ਸਹਿ ਸਕੈ ਜੀਭੈ ਛਾਲੈ ਅੰਝੂ ਰੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: saau na kauRaa seh sakai jeebhai chhaalai a(n)jhoo rovai|

en.bdb: Its bitter taste cannot be tolerated; it blisters the tongue and causes tears to trickle.
No garland is prepared of the oleander buds (for their being devoid of fragrance).
